subject: maths
question: In an election, Candidate A secures 60% of the votes, Candidate B secures 30% of the votes, and Candidate C secures the remaining 10%. If the total number of votes cast in the election is 1,20,000, how many more votes did Candidate A receive than Candidate B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference = (60% − 30%) of total

= 30% of 120000 = 36000

**∴ Answer = 36,000 votes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total votes = 1,20,000

A = 60%, B = 30%

**Formula used:**

Votes = (% × Total) / 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Votes of A = 60% of 120000 = 72000

⇒ Votes of B = 30% of 120000 = 36000

⇒ Difference = 72000 − 36000 = 36000

**∴ The correct answer is 36,000 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Concept

Percentage difference = difference of percentages × total

Quick Tip

Directly subtract percentages to save time
